$comment: Which blocks and which block states exist in which Minecraft version.
Generated and maintained by the `mc-block-versions` skill
(.claude/skills/mc-block-versions). `node scripts/gen-block-versions.mjs` turns this
into the table in src/shared/block_versions.ts; `--refresh` re-derives the `blocks`
and `properties` sections from the two sources before generating.
This is what makes a version change mean something. Without it, backporting a 1.21
schematic to 1.13 moved the tag and nothing else, leaving 501 kinds of block in a
file for a game that has never heard of them.
## Two sources, and the reason is not a principle
misode/mcmeta is the obvious source and it is the one this repo already uses for
block_states.json. On its own it would have been catastrophic here: its summary
lists ONLY blocks that have properties up to 1.20.4, and every block from 1.20.5
on -- 686 entries then 1060, with `stone` appearing at the boundary.
A plain diff of it therefore says `stone`, `dirt`, `cobblestone`, `oak_planks` and
some 370 others were introduced in 1.20.5. Acted on, backporting any build to 1.19
would replace every stone block in it with empty space -- a total loss, with the
look of a deliberate one, that no test written against the data itself could see.
So block presence comes from PrismarineJS/minecraft-data, which lists every block
at every version (verified: `stone` present in all 37 versions it covers, and zero
monotonicity gaps), and mcmeta corroborates where it is able to speak. The
`mc-versions` rule -- two independent sources, and absence is not disagreement --
arrived at from the data rather than from the principle.
## Which source answers which question
block presence   -> minecraft-data, corroborated by mcmeta   (`blocks`)
property names   -> minecraft-data, uniform coverage         (`properties`)
property VALUES  -> mcmeta ONLY                              (`propertyValues`)
That last line is a finding, not a preference. minecraft-data types an integer
property as `num_values` with no range, and its own count shifts between releases:
read naively it claims `snow.layers` went from 1..8 to 0..7 in 1.17 and back in
1.18, four times over, for a property the game has never changed. mcmeta lists the
values themselves, out of the game's own registry.
## What is derived and what is not
`blocks` and `properties` are diffed mechanically and re-checked by the generator.
`renames` and `propertyValues` are NOT: a diff sees `chain` disappear and
`iron_chain` appear, and cannot tell that from a removal plus an unrelated
addition. Getting it backwards is not a smaller version of being right -- it
replaces every chain in the build with empty space instead of renaming it. Those
rows are looked up, corroborated against the wiki's History section, and carry
their evidence.
`sources` on a block row records who could speak, not how sure we are. mcmeta is
absent from a row whenever its coverage could not settle the question -- which,
before 1.20.5, is every block that carries no properties.
Which versions each source covers, and how completely. The generator re-derives
this on --refresh and refuses if it has moved: a source that quietly changes what
it lists is exactly the failure this file exists to have caught once.

prismarine.note: Shares a directory between versions (1.16 -> pc/1.16.1, 1.18.2 -> pc/1.18, 1.21.10 -> pc/1.21.9), so its granularity is coarser than this app's version list. 1.21.7 is interpolated from 1.21.6 and 1.21.8, which mcmeta shows are identical.

mcmeta.note: Lists only blocks carrying properties before 1.20.5. Its silence there is absence of coverage, not absence of the block -- and a block that LOSES all its properties vanishes from it, which is why cauldron looks removed in 1.17 when it only lost level to water_cauldron.

evidence: minecraft.wiki/w/Oak_Sign History: the id changed from sign to oak_sign in 1.14 (18w43a), when every wood got its own sign.
minecraft-data: sign present through 1.13.2 and absent from 1.14; oak_sign first at 1.14.
The same 1.14 change, applied to the wall variant.
minecraft-data: wall_sign present through 1.13.2 and absent from 1.14; oak_wall_sign first at 1.14.
minecraft.wiki/w/Dirt_Path History: renamed from grass_path to dirt_path in 1.17 (20w45a).
minecraft-data: grass_path present through 1.16.5 and absent from 1.17; dirt_path first at 1.17.
minecraft.wiki/w/Short_Grass History, 1.20.3 Pre-Release 1: the ID of Grass, now Short Grass, has been changed from grass to short_grass.
minecraft-data: grass present through 1.20.2 and absent from 1.20.4; short_grass first at 1.20.4.
renames.note: The game renamed it in 1.20.3, which this app does not offer. 1.20.4 is the first version in MC_VERSIONS carrying the new name, and so the only boundary this file can act on.

evidence: minecraft.wiki/w/Iron_Chain History, 1.21.9 (25w35a): Renamed chain to iron_chain. Added in 1.16 (20w16a) as chain.
minecraft-data and mcmeta both: chain present 1.16 through 1.21.8; iron_chain and copper_chain first at 1.21.9.
renames.note: Renamed because copper_chain arrived beside it. Reported once as a 1.19 change, which it is not, and nothing local could have caught that.

propertyValues.lossy: tall -> true. Before 1.16 a wall had one height, so a tall connection comes back as an ordinary one: the wall survives, one block shorter. There is nothing else 1.15 can say.
evidence: minecraft.wiki/w/Wall History, 1.16 (20w06a): wall connection states changed from a boolean to none/low/tall.
mcmeta: all 14 walls carry north/south/east/west as true|false at 1.15.2 and none|low|tall at 1.16.

propertyValues.lossy: Every mob-head instrument becomes harp, the vanilla default. A note block that played a creeper plays a harp; there is nothing else to map it to.
evidence: minecraft.wiki/w/Note_Block History, 1.19.3 (22w42a): mob head instruments added.
mcmeta: note_block.instrument goes from 16 values at 1.19.2 to 23 at 1.19.3.

propertyValues.lossy: As above, for the trumpet instruments.
evidence: mcmeta: note_block.instrument goes from 23 values at 1.21.11 to 27 at 26.1, the four new ones being trumpet and its oxidation stages.

propertyValues.lossy: age=2 becomes age=1. This one narrows going FORWARD -- the crop lost a growth stage between 1.19.4 and 1.20 -- so here it is the backport that has nothing to do.
evidence: mcmeta: torchflower_crop.age is 0|1|2 at 1.19.4 and 0|1 at 1.20.
